cells.tense: You are standing in the field now, with the pen in your hand.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: The next small thing where no one can see whether you're fair — who gets the last of it, what you owe back — go with what feels right, then move on.
cells.core:
You can move through fog with only the next step lit, and you don't need the whole road. Part of that is a private sense of what's fair that shows up before you've argued it out. You don't run the numbers on the small stuff; you feel the right weight of it and act, and people get an even deal from you without ever seeing the scales. The fog doesn't seem to scramble that.

So use it where it's cheapest. Not a court case, not a family reckoning. The tip you leave, the thing you owe back, the split of the last piece that no one is watching. Go with what feels right and don't revisit it after. You'll find the compass doesn't need daylight to work. What it needs is a case small enough that you'll let it decide.
cells.sheetLine: You can move through fog, and you know what's fair before you argue it.
cells.verb: gathering what the change has grown
cells.place: in the part of life with only enough light for the next step

cells.tense: You'll be in the field before it's ripe, and the pen will already be moving.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Spend an hour with one thing that's settled in you, no task attached — no fixing it, no figuring out what it means for next month.
cells.core:
Where you gather what the change has grown, the reaping is running past the crop. You're reading the rows before they finish filling out, and the reading itself is the rush — what will it be, when will you know, will this be enough. Enough light for the next step has been turned into a demand for the whole field, and some of what's on the scale hasn't finished growing.

Push back the other way. Something settled doesn't need another pass. Choose the one you'd stake least on re-examining and give it a week off — not as strategy, as rest. The pull to check it again will arrive on schedule and will not mean anything. Feeling left to settle comes back with more, not less. The row you stopped reading will still be there, and fuller.
cells.sheetLine: Part of what's on the scale hasn't finished growing.

cells.tense: You passed the field a while back and haven't turned toward it since.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Take the piece that's been sitting there longest and do its next part at a pace you could carry a month through — that part only, no catch-up.
cells.core:
The fog is still here and you've stopped stepping into it. Where you gather what the change has grown, the survey isn't being made — not refused exactly, just not done, so the field has gone half-read while you stand at the edge taking in everything at once. You're not lazy and you're not lost. You're waiting for enough light to see the whole way before you go, and it doesn't work that way.

So move at a size you can hold. One part, at a pace you could carry a month through — not a burst, nothing heroic. Feeling will come alongside once the moving starts; it tends to. If the next step is genuinely too big, make it smaller instead of waiting. Walking is how the way has shown itself before, and you've done that.
cells.sheetLine: Make the next step small enough to take in the fog.

cells.tense: The field is gathered and you're calling the yield the weather's.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Say what you've organized out loud, once, in your own words — what the shape of it is and that you set it. No preamble, no apology, then move on.
cells.core:
You can stand in uncertainty and still hold the shape of a thing — what goes where, what comes first, what the order is — and part of that is your own sense of what's fair, working quietly. The structure holds. What's not holding is your name on it. The plans are being made, the rows are being ordered, the fair call is being made, and it's all getting filed under circumstance, or luck, or just how things worked out.

Say the shape out loud, once. Not a defense, not a case — what it is, and that you set it. Then stop talking and carry on with whatever comes next. What you'll notice is that nothing falls over. The structure was already carrying weight; it just wasn't being carried under your name. Naming it isn't pride. It's the plain report of who put it here, and the people standing on it know already.
cells.sheetLine: You drew the shape of it, so say so out loud.
cells.verb: gathering what the change has grown
cells.place: in the part of life with only enough light for the next step
